Le feu que personne ne laisse mourir. To: The fire nobody lets die. The rest of the village settled all around it.
Un poteau planté dans l'anse : quand un: A post planted in the cove: when a garment hangs from it, nobody fishes here any more.
Le rocher d'où l'on regarde le ciel au l: The rock from which you watch the sky at sunrise and sunset.
Un carré de terre retournée près de l'ea: A patch of turned earth near the water. People sow there on a trial basis, and watch what comes up.
Une salle basse où l'on pétrit l'argile: A low room where clay is kneaded and children copy signs from morning to night. Everything the island owes or owns is recorded there.
Une pierre dressée sur la place, où chac: A standing stone on the square, where anyone can read what is allowed and what it costs to forget it.
Un billot, deux coins gravés et un marte: A block, two engraved dies and a hammer: the island's tokens are struck there, all of the same weight, so metal no longer has to be weighed at every exchange.
Des bottes de tiges mises à sécher sous: Bundles of stems set to dry under an awning. The thread the island makes its ropes, nets and baskets from is twisted there.
Un tronc creusé au feu et à la hache, ti: A trunk hollowed out with fire and axe, pulled up on the sand. With it, you fish farther than the shore and bring back what the island doesn't have.
